code_review.project_type: full-stack web application — React/Vite SPA gallery + FastAPI REST/SSE backend showcasing eight AI application patterns

existing_self_description.text: Built with Spec4 (BWS4) is a living showcase of common AI application patterns, presented as a collection of small, self-contained example apps behind a single landing page. Each example demonstrates one pattern end-to-end: how it's built, what it depends on, and how it behaves, so that visitors unfamiliar with the underlying technique can understand it by seeing it work rather than by reading about it abstractly.

architecture.summary: Vertical-slice modular monolith: each example app owns a backend slice package (schemas/service/validator/versioned Markdown prompts) exposed through a deliberately thin FastAPI router, and all slices draw on one shared framework layer for model calls, embeddings, web search, storage, moderation and usage gating. The React SPA mirrors the same partitioning with per-example lazy-loaded route chunks.
architecture.pattern: vertical-slice modular monolith over a shared service layer

languages.name: Markdown (prompt templates and RAG dataset used as data)

protocols_implemented.name: A2A (Agent2Agent Protocol) — data model and interaction pattern only, no network transport

api_surface.summary: Serves three A2A-shaped agent cards from module constants with camelCase alias serialisation; no model, DB or quota use
SSE stream of the negotiation, one event per stage, 15s keep-alive pings, DB session opened inside the generator
Runs the two-call writer/critic chain; a failed second call returns 200 with status 'critique_failed' rather than an error
Describes the chain's steps and roles before it runs, built from the pipeline's own constants
Liveness endpoint that must stay up independent of example-app failures

ai_capabilities.name: litellm
ai_capabilities.description: Primary model lane: every example app's generation call goes through one registry that walks an ordered chain of free-tier OpenRouter/Groq models on failure and benches withdrawn slugs

ai_capabilities.name: pydantic-ai
ai_capabilities.description: Second model lane used where an app wants framework-bound, validated typed output instead of parsing JSON out of prose; reads slugs from the same registry and passes the same usage gate

ai_capabilities.name: sentence-transformers
ai_capabilities.description: In-process all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings powering the embeddings example's 24 presets and all RAG chunk/query embedding; deliberately uncapped since it spends no third-party quota

ai_capabilities.name: torch
ai_capabilities.description: Local inference runtime backing sentence-transformers, loaded at boot in the FastAPI lifespan

ai_capabilities.name: pgvector
ai_capabilities.description: dataset_embeddings table with an HNSW index queried by cosine distance through SQLAlchemy for RAG retrieval

ai_capabilities.name: BWS4 RAG pipeline
ai_capabilities.description: Hand-rolled sentence-aligned overlapping chunking, title-prepended passage embedding, retrieval, grounded answer generation, and a citation audit that verifies cited passages were actually retrieved

ai_capabilities.name: scikit-learn
ai_capabilities.description: PCA fitted once at startup over the curated preset embeddings and thereafter only applied, so existing plot points never move when a visitor adds text

ai_capabilities.name: Exa
ai_capabilities.description: Live web-search API exposed as a shared framework capability and invoked by the tool-use example's function-calling loop

ai_capabilities.name: BWS4 collab negotiation runtime
ai_capabilities.description: Buyer agent negotiates one procurement round against two rival sellers over a fixed 8 model calls, with opacity enforced structurally by assembling each turn only from messages addressed to that agent

ai_capabilities.name: BWS4 orchestrated subagents runtime
ai_capabilities.description: Coordinator selects two of four fixed specialists, writes each a distinct brief, runs both concurrently and merges their answers

ai_capabilities.name: BWS4 planning agent
ai_capabilities.description: Planner call decomposes a trip-day goal into an approvable plan; execution is a separate API call so the human-in-the-loop checkpoint cannot be defaulted away

ai_capabilities.name: sentry-sdk
ai_capabilities.description: Performance spans around LLM calls plus error tracking on both tiers, no-oping cleanly when no DSN is configured

test_coverage.coverage_summary: Backend tests live under backend/tests/ (pyproject testpaths) and frontend tests run via vitest; the tests directory listing was truncated so per-module coverage could not be determined. One documented assertion: the collab identity-cards endpoint's test asserts A2A camelCase alias serialisation rather than trusting configuration.

incomplete_or_dead_code: uv run ruff check . does not lint most of the backend: [tool.ruff] extend-exclude exempts main.py, eight of nine API routers, and the chained_calls, core, db, embeddings, planning and rag packages plus most of services/ — the manifest states ruff reports 366 findings and would reformat 57 files across those paths, so a green lint run is not evidence the touched code is clean.
mypy strict coverage is scoped the same way: pre-v6 routers inherit an exemption, so a new or edited file must be added to the gate explicitly or it is silently unchecked.
The structured single-call mode has a known provider gap: 2 of the 8 free models in the chain do not honour a JSON Schema directive, so non-conforming raw output is reported as a failure by design.

frontend/package.json declares the full plotly.js package while README states only the ~1 MB plotly-basic build ships, so the slimming depends on an import path/alias that is not expressed in the manifest and can regress silently into a ~4.7 MB bundle.

change_risks.area: free-tier model fallback chains in backend/app/services/model_registry.py
change_risks.risk: README states the per-capability chains rot as providers retire free slugs, so both the tool-calling and text-generation chains go stale over time
change_risks.mitigation_hint: refresh slugs with backend/app/services/discover_models.py and probe_capabilities.py and edit only model_registry.py; never hard-code a slug in a slice, since both the LiteLLM and PydanticAI lanes read this one registry

change_risks.risk: the SSE response outlives the request handler, so a Depends(get_db_session) session is closed while the generator is still writing
change_risks.mitigation_hint: open the session inside the async generator with async_session_factory, following backend/app/api/collab.py; do not add the DB dependency to a streaming route

change_risks.risk: ensure_built() failures are swallowed by a bare except Exception (noqa BLE001) so a broken embeddings projection shows up only as a slow first request, and anything added to lifespan compounds an already large torch + sentence-transformers cold start
change_risks.mitigation_hint: keep warm-up best-effort but assert on the embeddings_projection_warmup_failed log event in tests, and avoid adding new blocking work to lifespan

change_risks.risk: a failed second call returns HTTP 200 with status 'critique_failed' so clients must branch on the body; converting it to 4xx/5xx would push the client error branch and discard call 1's output
change_risks.mitigation_hint: preserve the 200-with-status contract and keep CHAIN_LENGTH/ROLE_* imported from the pipeline so the advertised plan and executed roles cannot drift

change_risks.area: hand-maintained ruff/mypy exclusion inventories in pyproject.toml
change_risks.risk: the exclusion lists are per-file by design; a new file added inside an already-excluded package is silently ungated, and un-excluding a legacy path surfaces a large batch of findings at once
change_risks.mitigation_hint: add each new file to the gate explicitly and clean up one excluded path at a time by deleting its single line, as the manifest comments instruct

security_observations: Unauthenticated public API by design; abuse control is per-UTC-hour usage caps enforced before any provider call, plus moderation.py, text_gate.py, allowance_holds.py and an untrusted.py boundary for visitor-supplied text
CORS restricted to exactly one configured origin (settings.cors_origin), never '*' (backend/app/main.py)
Secrets are declared sync: false in render.yaml and entered in the Render dashboard rather than committed

Agent opacity in the collab example is enforced structurally — a seller's turn is assembled only from messages addressed to it, so a rival's price is unreachable even under prompt attack, and the message log lets a visitor verify no seller-to-seller traffic
Browser localStorage stores theme preference only and is explicitly not a source of truth
other_notes: Frontend tests: `npm --prefix frontend run test` (vitest run)
Frontend production preview: `npm --prefix frontend run preview`
Database migrations: `uv run alembic upgrade head` (config at backend/alembic.ini)
Backend reload dev mode: `uv run uvicorn backend.app.main:app --reload`
Production start command lives in render.yaml's startCommand, which was truncated in the sampled excerpt

render.yaml defines two targets: bws4-api (type: web, runtime: python, plan: starter, region: oregon, rootDir: .) and a CDN-served Render Static Site for the web client; starter rather than free is chosen because the api pays a large cold start loading torch and sentence-transformers then fitting PCA in lifespan
No Dockerfile, docker-compose, Kubernetes manifests or Terraform anywhere in the tree
`.python-version` and `.env.example` present at repo root; a single root `.env` configures both the backend and the frontend
CLA.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CLAUDE.md and LICENSE are present but their contents were not sampled, so no commands were drawn from them
Prompts are file-based and versioned as Markdown (prompts/*_v1.md, rag/prompts/answer_v2.md) with dedicated loaders in three packages plus services/prompt_context.py
Every source file opens with the provenance comment `# Built with Spec4 AI - https://spec4.ai` (or `//` in TypeScript)
render.yaml cites .spec4/v0/stack.json as the origin of the deployment shape, indicating the repo is maintained through the Spec4 workflow across revisions v0 through v6

The A2A trust boundary is described candidly in-product as staged for teaching, since all three agents ship under one owner; the collab run costs a fixed 8 model calls (6 negotiation + 2 post-award explanation)
TypeScript uses project references: frontend/tsconfig.json points to tsconfig.app.json and tsconfig.node.json
